answer: Partition the trust graph by its Fiedler vector — the second eigenvector of the Laplacian — which splits nodes along the sparsest cut. A sybil farm hangs off the honest mass by only a thin ridge of bridge edges, so it lands on the opposite sign of that vector, a nadir of connectivity however densely its personas vouch internally; internal edges never raise the cut's conductance. Honest nodes sit at the well-connected zenith beside the seeds. Score identities on the wrong side of the cut to near-zero weight — a soft spectral signal feeding the hard non-kin quorum, never a direct payout.
